card: Adds a -reobfuscate-blocks startup option allowing node operators to rewrite existing block and undo files under a new or random XOR key. Datadirs synced prior to Bitcoin Core v28 remain unobfuscated, leaving them vulnerable to false-positive file corruption by antivirus software unless the user resyncs the chain from scratch. The migration is crash-safe, preserves file timestamps, and can be resumed if interrupted. No dependencies are noted.
evidence: PR description: 'Nodes that synced before v28 may store block and undo files effectively unobfuscated with a zero XOR key. There is no built-in way to obfuscate those existing files, rotate their key, or deliberately replace it with a zero key without resyncing.'

PR description benchmarks show migration across hardware ranging from 10 minutes (Apple M4 Max SSD, ~854 GB) to 24 hours (Raspberry Pi 4 HDD, ~730 GB), demonstrating real-world viability on large datadirs.
References prior external implementations and PRs attempting to address the same limitation: PR #32451 and the standalone andrewtoth/blocks-xor tool.
problem: Nodes synced prior to Bitcoin Core v28 store block and undo files with a zero XOR key (unobfuscated), leaving them susceptible to antivirus scanners misidentifying block data and quarantining or deleting files. Node operators currently have no native way to obfuscate existing files, rotate their key, or remove obfuscation without redownloading the entire blockchain.

risk.why: Modifies and rewrites raw block and undo files on disk; an unhandled I/O error or staging bug could corrupt block storage and require reindexing or redownloading blocks.

scope_notes: Modifies startup flow in init.cpp before chainstate loading, refactors DirectoryCommit fs helper to report failure, and restructures block/rev file scanning in blockstorage.
summary: Adds a `-reobfuscate-blocks[=<value>]` startup option to rewrite existing block and undo files (`blk*.dat` and `rev*.dat`) under a new random or user-specified XOR key. The migration runs single-threaded before chainstate loading, rewriting files in chunks to staged temporary files with disk commits to ensure crash safety and resumability. It also reports migration progress via log output and kernel progress notifications.
